name: Bambam
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 6 other works read were silent
catalog_quote: Stress in PUS is not phonemic. It normally occurs on the penultimate syllable of words or on the nucleus of the rare one-syllable roots. The addition of any suffixes to the word (thus making a new word) affects the placement of stress; that is, it causes the stress to shift to the right.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed penultimate, word domain excluding clitics) rests on the best and only dedicated phonology of the language, Campbell 1991 (SIL WILC 12, 52 pp), written by the resident fieldworker; the deciding quotation was verified verbatim at printed p.11 §3.1 of the PDF we hold, and the same statement appears in the held 1989 MA thesis §2.2 p.15. Campbell's qualifications (vocatives final-stressed; enclitics outside the stress domain; suffixes shift stress rightward, i.e. penult of the suffixed word) are consistent with the 'fixed-strict' penult rule string and the word domain note already in the domain locator. Glottolog lists no other grammar/phonology and a web search found no newer instrumental or descriptive study, so no better source exists to hold; nothing open was available to download (Smith 1993 is comparative and its MPG PuRe PDF is access-restricted).
